label: National Energy Emergency Status
source: Office of the President, Executive Order 110
delta: In effect since March 24, 2026. Instead of a spot-market suspension, ERC ordered (Sept 10) a regional WESM price cap — computed separately per region rather than system-wide — cutting simulated August spot prices 54% in Visayas (₱18.59→₱8.47/kWh) and 56% in Mindanao (₱19.56→₱8.69/kWh); IEMOP is recalculating August bills, due to utilities by Sept 20, and PEMC opened a 60-day probe into generator bidding behavior. The Visayas grid slipped back to yellow alert (4-8pm) Sept 21 and was hit with a further 1-hour red alert (5-6pm) on Sept 22 after the 56.6MW Palinpinon-2 geothermal plant tripped, on top of continued Therma Visayas Unit 1, PEDC Unit 3 and Kepco SPC Unit 2 outages (2,487MW available vs 2,550MW peak demand). The Mindanao grid, by contrast, returned to normal operating status Sept 23 as GNPower Kauswagan and Therma South units resynchronized (2,984MW available vs 2,656MW peak demand). Fuel prices rose a third time this month effective Sept 22 (diesel +₱8.82/L, gasoline +₱4.88/L, kerosene +₱6.47/L; national average ~₱102.78/L diesel, ~₱90.35/L gasoline as of Sept 23), driven by drone-attack damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline and the wider Middle East conflict; 3-week cumulative increase now ₱18.31/L diesel, ₱15.25/L gasoline. Separately, a tropical depression (~1,810km east of SE Luzon) is forecast to enter PAR Sept 24 as tropical storm 'Queenie', the 17th cyclone of 2026, threatening to further enhance the habagat over disaster-hit areas.
